title: University of Canterbury Doctoral Scholarship
deadline_note: The October round is for students intending to start doctoral studies before 1 July 2027. Students intending to start on or after 1 July 2027 must apply in the next round, which opens 20 March and closes 15 May. Applications are not accepted outside the published round dates.
application_cycle: Two rounds a year: October (opens 20 August, closes 15 October) and May (opens 20 March, closes 15 May)
status_note: The University of Canterbury publishes the October round as open for applications.
tuition_coverage_note: UC states the scholarship consists of financial assistance to a value of $32,650 per 120 points plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment for up to a total of 360 points.
benefits: Financial assistance to a value of $32,650 per 120 points
Tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment for up to a total of 360 points
Three Prestige top-up awards added automatically to the core value
Canterbury Scholarship for outstanding leadership and contribution (recognition only, no additional cash)
eligibility: Those with a GPA of 7.0 over the last two years of relevant degree study, in any discipline
Students undertaking their first research doctoral degree
International students are welcome to apply, unless restricted by the University's commercial arrangements with sponsors
Applicants must have a myUC account
Applicants must have submitted a separate application to study at UC before the scholarship closing date
requirements: Submit a separate admission application to UC before the scholarship closing date
Apply using the UC Doctoral Scholarship application form
International applicants must send certified scanned copies of academic transcripts, including Scholaro reports for preliminary and secondary school and tertiary study, and Course Descriptions
Supply referees' contact details for a written report and, if required, an interview
Submit ACT/SAT scores only if not previously supplied
coverage: Financial assistance to a value of $32,650 per 120 points
Tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment up to a total of 360 points
application_method: Apply online using the UC Doctoral Scholarship application form
A single application form covers the other Core scholarships except the UCDS for Students with Disabilities and UC Connect
application_route: One online application form covers the UC Doctoral Scholarship and, apart from UCDS for Students with Disabilities and UC Connect, the other Core scholarships.
duration: Up to 360 points of thesis-only doctoral study
description: The University of Canterbury Doctoral Scholarship consists of financial assistance to a value of $32,650 per 120 points plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment for up to a total of 360 points, with additional Prestige top-up awards available for outstanding doctoral students.

not_confirmed: documents (a full document list is not published on the page; the items listed are the ones the page does name)
verification.notes: Core value, 120-point cadence, 360-point tuition-fee coverage, GPA threshold, round dates and the Prestige top-up awards were read directly from the University of Canterbury Doctoral Scholarships page. Prestige top-ups are added automatically to the core value of the UC Doctoral Scholarship; the Canterbury Scholarship is described as recognition only. Full document requirements are set out in UC's scholarship application guidance rather than on this page.

applicant_utility: Read the Canterbury award as a per-120-point figure, not a single lump sum: $32,650 is attached to each 120-point block of thesis-only enrolment, so over a 360-point doctorate it is three blocks plus your tuition fees. The headline $32,650 is UC's core value; the Prestige top-ups are added automatically rather than applied for separately, with the Brownlie Scholarship adding $5,000 per 120 points and the Roper Scholarship in Science offering $30,000 per 120 points, which is why some Canterbury doctoral students end up far better funded than the base figure suggests. The application window is unforgiving - the October round for anyone starting before 1 July 2027 closed on 15 October 2026 and no applications are accepted outside the published rounds - and you must already have your admission application in before the scholarship closes. Allow six to eight weeks for a decision, and expect a written report from referees and possibly an interview as part of the review.

title: AUT Doctoral Scholarship
deadline_note: There are three closing dates in 2026: 1 March, 15 July and 1 November. Applications open one month before each closing date, and are accepted at any stage during the year apart from 1 December to 15 January for the Vice-Chancellor's Doctoral Scholarship. The next round opens 20 March 2026 with applications closing 15 May 2026.
application_cycle: Three closing dates a year (1 March, 15 July, 1 November), each with an intake opening one month before
status_note: AUT publishes the 1 November 2026 round, with applications open from 1 October 2026.
tuition_coverage_note: AUT states that each AUT Doctoral Scholarship consists of an annual stipend of $34,737 for 2026 awards, plus tuition fees and compulsory student services fee for up to three years of full-time study, or an annual stipend of $17,368.50 plus tuition fees and compulsory student services fee for up to six years of part-time study.
benefits: Tuition fees for the duration of the scholarship
Part-time option at a half-rate stipend ($17,368.50) with fees covered for up to six years
eligibility: Excellent academic record, normally first-class honours or equivalent
Potential for high-quality research in your chosen discipline
Open to all applicants, including those from countries other than New Zealand, provided admission requirements are met
Applicants must have received an Offer of Place from AUT
requirements: Apply for admission first - allow up to two months for international applications before the relevant closing date
Register on the AUT portal and add your documents
Submit a research statement of no more than 2 pages plus references (up to 1,000 words in total)
Submit a recent CV of up to 3 A4 pages
Provide transcripts for all non-AUT study
Two academic referees must submit their confidential reports directly to AUT
Obtain a support letter from an AUT faculty member where your proposed supervisor or Head of School is not a referee
Applications missing supporting documents will not be forwarded to the panel
application_method: Upload all documents through the AUT online application portal
application_route: Admission application first, then a separate doctoral scholarship application through the AUT portal with all documents uploaded.
study_mode: Full-time for three years, or part-time for six years at a half-rate stipend
duration: Up to three years of full-time study, or up to six years of part-time study
description: AUT doctoral scholarships attract and recognise highly achieving research students and stimulate doctoral research in areas that enhance AUT's capability, consisting of an annual stipend of $34,737 for 2026 awards plus tuition fees and the compulsory student services fee.

verification.notes: Stipend for 2026 awards, fee coverage, eligibility, application requirements and closing dates were read directly from the AUT doctoral scholarships page. AUT offers two distinct doctoral scholarships: the AUT Doctoral Scholarship, which is open to all applicants including those from other countries and requires an Offer of Place, and the Vice-Chancellor's Doctoral Scholarship, which is for new doctoral candidates holding at least a GPA of 8.0 or 7.5 for Maori or Pacific applicants - the Vice-Chancellor's medal is considered separately.

applicant_utility: AUT's package is one of the most complete in New Zealand: the stipend, the tuition fees and even the compulsory student services fee are covered, which removes the small surprise fees that other scholarships leave behind. The figure quoted, $34,737, is the 2026 award rate, so confirm the rate when your award is issued. Two practical hurdles. First, you must already hold an Offer of Place, so for international applicants AUT tells you to allow up to two months before the closing date - applying for admission and the scholarship in the same week is the most common reason people miss out. Second, the application is judged on the documents you upload: a research statement capped at two pages plus references, a CV of no more than three A4 pages, transcripts for all non-AUT study, and two academics who report to AUT directly rather than through you. If your proposed supervisor or Head of School is not one of your referees, you need a support letter from an AUT faculty member as well. Part-time study is possible, but at $17,368.50 a year the stipend halves while fees are still covered.
